snapshot.title: TNPSC Polity: Union Executive & Parliament
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Polity Hook: 35: Age. 110: Money. 108: Joint. 76: AG. 123: Ordinance. 72: Pardon.

quick_notes.title: The President (Art 52)
quick_notes.detail: Nominal Head. Elected by Electoral College. Pardoning power (Art 72). Ordinance (Art 123). Min Age : 35.
quick_notes.explanation: The President of India, as described in Article 52 of the Constitution, is the official head of the country but does not have real executive power, meaning they are a nominal head whose role is mostly ceremonial. The President is not directly elected by the people; instead, they are chosen by an Electoral College, which is a group of voters made up of all elected members of both the Parliament and the State Legislative Assemblies. To be eligible for this office, a person must be at least 35 years old. Article 72 gives the President the power to grant pardons, which means they can forgive or reduce a person's punishment for a crime. Article 123 allows the President to issue an ordinance, which is a temporary law that has the same force as an Act of Parliament, but only when Parliament is not in session.

quick_notes.title: Prime Minister
quick_notes.detail: Real Head. Appointed by President. Head of Council of Ministers. Term : Pleasure of President.
quick_notes.explanation: The Prime Minister is the real head of the government, meaning they actually run the country, while the President is only the ceremonial head. The President formally appoints the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers, which is the group of senior ministers who make major decisions. The Prime Minister's term lasts as long as the President is "pleased" with them, but in practice this means until the Prime Minister loses the support of a majority in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of Parliament.

quick_notes.title: Parliament (Art 79)
quick_notes.detail: Lok Sabha (People's House - max 550). Rajya Sabha (States' House - max 250). RS is a permanent house.
quick_notes.explanation: Article 79 of the Indian Constitution establishes that Parliament has three parts: the President, the Lok Sabha, and the Rajya Sabha. Lok Sabha, short for House of the People, is the lower house; its maximum strength is 550 members, all directly elected by Indian citizens. Rajya Sabha, short for Council of States, is the upper house; its maximum strength is 250 members, most of whom are elected by the state legislative assemblies. Unlike the Lok Sabha, which is dissolved every five years, the Rajya Sabha is a permanent house that never dissolves, but one-third of its members retire every two years.

quick_notes.title: Parliamentary Terms
quick_notes.detail: Joint Sitting (Art 108). Money Bill (Art 110 - only in LS). Annual Financial Statement/Budget (Art 112).
quick_notes.explanation: A Joint Sitting is a special meeting of both houses of Parliament together, called under Article 108 to resolve a deadlock when one house rejects or disagrees with a bill passed by the other house. A Money Bill is a bill that deals only with taxes, government borrowing, or spending from the Consolidated Fund of India, and under Article 110 it can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, which is the lower house of Parliament. The Annual Financial Statement, commonly called the Budget, is a document presented under Article 112 that shows the government's estimated income and expenses for the upcoming financial year.

quick_notes.title: Attorney General (Art 76)
quick_notes.detail: Highest Law Officer. Appointed by President. Right to speak in both houses but NO vote.
quick_notes.explanation: The Attorney General of India, as stated in Article 76 of the Constitution, is the government's top legal advisor, meaning they are the highest law officer for the country. This person is chosen and appointed by the President of India, who is the head of state. The Attorney General has the right to speak and take part in discussions in both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, which are the two houses of the Indian Parliament, but they do not have the right to vote on any matter.
